countries.summary: Ireland's energy regulator, the CRU, set a connection policy for large energy users (mostly data centres) in December 2025, replacing the earlier reactive approach. Per secondary law-firm summaries, the policy applies to new connection applications, sorts projects by maximum import capacity, and ties larger connections to new on-site or nearby generation or storage and to renewable investment; the primary CRU decision paper has not been read. The Greater Dublin Area is described by the policy source as the most constrained area. The CSO reports that data centres used 23% of metered electricity in 2025.

context.statement: Data centres accounted for 23% of metered electricity consumption in Ireland in 2025, up from 5% in 2015.

countries.summary: UK planning is decided by local planning authorities or, for large projects, through the nationally significant infrastructure regime. The government's AI Growth Zones policy paper of 13 November 2025 sets out grid capacity reservation and reallocation mechanisms and a geographic electricity price discount for data centres in designated zones. Local disputes include Nscale's Loughton scheme in Epping Forest, where council officers asked for a new application.

France's grid connection and siting rules are set nationally, with the transmission operator RTE, and locally through planning. In June 2026 the Île-de-France region adopted a regional siting strategy that would move grid connection priority to a 'first ready, first served' logic and renegotiate the financial deal with local authorities; it is described as a plan whose binding force is not stated on the fetched page. The region holds 44% of the 322 data centres recorded in France at end-2024.

countries.summary: EU-level rules reach all member states. The recast Energy Efficiency Directive requires reporting on data-centre energy performance, and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 sets the information and indicators for that reporting and a common rating scheme. The Commission's Cloud and AI Development Act proposal of June 2026 would create data-centre acceleration zones with a 12-month permit cap, but that proposal is still in the legislative process and its details were not read from the Commission text.

fields.title: CRU Large Energy User (LEU) connection policy decision
fields.identifier: CRU/2025236 (from secondary sources only; not confirmed on cru.ie)
fields.summary: Regulator decision for large energy users, mostly data centres, seeking a new grid connection. Projects are sorted by maximum import capacity (below 1 MVA exempt; 1 to 10 MVA; above 10 MVA). Above 10 MVA the policy requires proximate or behind-the-meter generation sized to 100% of the grid connection, and renewable investment matching 80% of annual demand per the DCByte summary. Applications made before the decision date are assessed under earlier policy. The Greater Dublin Area is described as the most constrained area.
key_terms: segmenting projects by maximum import capacity: <1 MVA, 1–10 MVA, and >10 MVA.

fields.title: Delivering AI Growth Zones (policy paper)
fields.summary: Government policy paper for AI Growth Zones, designated locations for AI compute investment. It proposes a reservation mechanism that holds grid capacity at a specific connection point, a reallocation mechanism for capacity freed when a project leaves the queue, and removal of speculative demand from the connections queue. It also proposes geographic electricity price support, for a 500 MW data centre up to £24/MWh in Scotland, £16/MWh in Cumbria and £14/MWh in the North East, delivered as an electricity-cost discount tied to demonstrated savings.
key_terms: a reservation mechanism that allows capacity to be held at a specific physical connection point
a reallocation mechanism that gives priority access to freed-up capacity when another project exits the queue
Where data centres in AI Growth Zones facilitate these savings, they will receive a commensurate discount on electricity costs.

fields.title: Île-de-France regional strategy for siting data centres
fields.summary: Regional siting strategy for data centres, adopted 25 June 2026. It aims to maximise local spin-offs and to renegotiate the financial deal with local authorities, and proposes moving grid connection priority from 'first come, first served' to 'first ready, first served'. The fetched article calls it a strategy whose binding force is not stated; it describes planned actions such as an observatory and a methodological kit.
